text: Imagine hiccupping for sixty-eight years. A hiccup is your diaphragm, the big muscle under your lungs, suddenly twitching. Air rushes in, and a flap in your throat slams shut. Hic! In nineteen twenty-two, an American farmer named Charles Osborne fell while lifting a hog, and started hiccupping. He kept going for sixty-eight years. Up to forty times a minute at first. That's an estimated four hundred and thirty million hiccups. Then, about a year before he died, they just... stopped. What's your best hiccup cure?
